source.english_context: Unit 24 Lost Items, Help Desks, and Service Problems Goal: explain a problem calmly, ask for the next step, and keep proof. Daily Life English I lost my wallet. Who should I speak with? Can I get a case number? Could you please write that down for me? I last saw it near the front entrance. It is a black backpack with a red tag. Has anyone turned in a set of keys? When should I check back? Could you confirm my contact details? The item I received is damaged. This is not the service I ordered. Can you tell me what happens next? How long does this usually take to resolve? Could you send me a written confirmation? Thank you for looking into this. Vocabulary help desk a place or person who helps with problems lost and found a place for missing items case number a number used to track a problem manager a person who can make decisions complaint a report about a problem follow up contact again later about the same issue description words that explain what something looks like or is like contact details information such as a phone number or email address proof of purchase a record showing that you bought an item replacement something provided in place of a lost or damaged item resolve find an answer or solution to a problem turn in give a found item to staff or another responsible person US Customs Stay calm and specific. Say what happened, when it happened, and what you need now. Ask for a receipt, email, ticket number, or case number after reporting a problem. If the first person cannot help, politely ask who can make the decision. Describe a lost item with details such as its color, size, and a distinctive feature. Avoid giving only a general name. For a billing or order problem, have the receipt or order number ready. Explain the difference between what you expected and received. Ask when and how you should follow up, and write down the contact details so you reach the correct team. Before ending the conversation, repeat the agreed next step. A clear summary helps both you and the staff member avoid misunderstandings. Dialogue Student: Excuse me, I left my backpack on the bus. Staff: What bus route and what time? Student: Route 12 at about 4:30 p.m. Staff: Please fill out this lost item form. Student: Thank you. Can I get a case number? Staff: Yes. It is 318. What does the backpack look like? Student: It is dark green with a small yellow patch on the front. Staff: Please add that description and your contact number to the form. Student: When should I check back if I have not heard anything? Staff: Call this office tomorrow afternoon and give us your case number.

japanese_explanation.heading: 問題は落ち着いて、具体的に伝える
points: 困った時は、何が起きたか、いつ起きたか、今何をしてほしいかを短く伝えます。
case number、receipt、email、ticket number は後で確認するために大切です。必ずメモや写真で残しましょう。
最初の人が助けられない時は、怒らずに Who should I speak with? と聞くと次につながりやすいです。
japanese_explanation.practice: Can I get a case number?

existing_simplified_chinese.heading: 遇到问题要冷静、具体地说明
points: 有问题时，简短说明发生了什么、什么时候发生、现在需要对方做什么。
case number、receipt、email 和 ticket number 对后续查询很重要，要保存或拍照。
如果第一个人不能帮忙，不要生气。问 Who should I speak with? 会更容易找到负责的人。
existing_simplified_chinese.practice: Can I get a case number?

ja.heading: 問題は落ち着いて、具体的に伝える
points: 困った時は、何が起きたか、いつ起きたか、今何をしてほしいかを短く伝えます。
case number、receipt、email、ticket number は後で確認するために大切です。必ずメモや写真で残しましょう。
最初の人が助けられない時は、怒らずに Who should I speak with? と聞くと次につながりやすいです。

ko.heading: 문제를 침착하게 구체적으로 설명하기
points: 문제가 생겼을 때는 무엇이 일어났는지, 언제 일어났는지, 지금 무엇을 원하는지 간결하게 설명하세요.
case number, receipt, email, ticket number는 나중에 확인하기 위해 중요합니다. 반드시 메모하거나 사진으로 남겨두세요.
첫 번째 담당자가 도와줄 수 없을 때는 화내지 않고 Who should I speak with? 라고 물으면 다음 단계로 나아가기 쉽습니다.

zh-Hans.heading: 遇到问题要冷静、具体地说明
points: 有问题时，简短说明发生了什么、什么时候发生、现在需要对方做什么。
case number、receipt、email 和 ticket number 对后续查询很重要，要保存或拍照。
如果第一个人不能帮忙，不要生气。问 Who should I speak with? 会更容易找到负责的人。

es.heading: Comunique el problema con calma y de forma específica
points: Cuando tenga un problema, explique brevemente qué pasó, cuándo pasó y qué necesita ahora.
Los datos como case number, receipt, email o ticket number son importantes para futuras referencias. Asegúrese de anotarlos o tomarles una foto.
Si la primera persona no puede ayudarle, pregunte con calma "Who should I speak with?" (¿Con quién debo hablar?) para que le deriven a la persona adecuada.

pt-BR.heading: Comunique o problema com calma e de forma específica
points: Quando tiver um problema, explique brevemente o que aconteceu, quando aconteceu e o que você precisa agora.
O case number, o receipt, o email e o ticket number são importantes para consultas futuras. Certifique-se de anotá-los ou tirar uma foto.
Se a primeira pessoa não puder ajudar, pergunte calmamente "Who should I speak with?" (Com quem devo falar?) para facilitar o próximo passo.

fr.heading: Décrire le problème calmement et précisément
points: Lorsque vous rencontrez un problème, expliquez brièvement ce qui s'est passé, quand cela s'est produit et ce dont vous avez besoin maintenant.
Des éléments comme le case number, le receipt, l'email ou le ticket number sont importants pour un suivi ultérieur. Assurez-vous de les noter ou de les photographier.
Si la première personne ne peut pas vous aider, demandez calmement « Who should I speak with? » (À qui dois-je parler ?) pour faciliter la progression.

de.heading: Schildern Sie das Problem ruhig und präzise
points: Wenn Sie ein Problem haben, beschreiben Sie kurz, was passiert ist, wann es passiert ist und was Sie jetzt brauchen.
Eine case number, ein receipt, eine email oder eine ticket number sind für spätere Nachfragen wichtig. Stellen Sie sicher, dass Sie diese notieren oder fotografieren.
Wenn die erste Person Ihnen nicht helfen kann, fragen Sie ruhig „Who should I speak with?“ (Mit wem sollte ich sprechen?), um den nächsten Schritt zu erleichtern.
